title: Factors, multiples, primes and square numbers
canonical_examples_source: Arithmetic self-verified; method ref: NCERT Class 5/6 Maths; format ref: bank uk-ks2-2024 maths.

blocks.content: Numbers have families. Factors and multiples describe how numbers fit together, and special numbers like primes and squares have patterns worth knowing.
A factor divides a number exactly, with no remainder. A multiple is what you get when you multiply a number by a whole number.

steps: 12 divided by 3 is exactly 4, so 3 is a factor of 12.
3 x 1 = 3, 3 x 2 = 6, 3 x 3 = 9, so 3, 6 and 9 are multiples of 3.

blocks.prompt: Is 4 a factor of 12? Work out 12 ÷ 4 = ___
blocks.explain: 12 ÷ 4 = 3 with no remainder, so 4 is a factor of 12.
blocks.rule: A number is a factor if it divides exactly, leaving no remainder.

practiceItems.prompt: the smallest factor of any number

blocks.content: A prime number has exactly two factors: 1 and itself. A square number is a number multiplied by itself (like 4 x 4 = 16).

blocks.question: Which of these is a prime number?
blocks.explain: 7 has only two factors, 1 and 7, so it is prime. (9 = 3 x 3 and 12 has many factors.)
blocks.rule: A prime number has exactly two factors: 1 and itself.

blocks.content: Factors divide exactly, multiples come from multiplying, primes have just two factors, and squares are a number times itself. Let's practise!
